meta.title: Suggestion register — paths to choose from before anything is implemented
meta.how_to_choose: Each suggestion lists 2-3 mutually exclusive paths. Pick ONE path per suggestion. The recommendation column is the engine's opinion, not a decision; the owner decides. Nothing here has been implemented yet unless the status says so.

status_legend.proposed: not started — awaiting a path choice
status_legend.implemented: built and verified in this session
status_legend.blocked: cannot start until a named dependency exists

suggestions.title: Write a source contract for every official page we use
suggestions.problem: Right now each dataset was captured by hand once. There is no written agreement about which page owns which field, or what happens when a page changes shape.
suggestions.implemented_note: data/sources.json now records publisher, fields used, verification state and a rejection list. The refresh job (SG-02) enforces it.

paths.name: Hand-curated registry
paths.pros: Exact, reviewable, no scraping fragility beyond the four pages we already read.
paths.cons: Breaks silently if NFL.com renames a column.

paths.name: Scrape everything with selectors
paths.pros: More fields per page.
paths.cons: Every selector is a liability; no SLA; likely violates nothing but is fragile.

paths.name: Buy a data vendor
paths.pros: Stable schema.
paths.cons: No longer an 'official source' claim; costs money.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Accept that four hand-verified pages are the foundation, or approve a vendor budget.

suggestions.title: Freeze the line at kickoff and never edit it
suggestions.problem: An originated line is worthless for grading if it can be quietly improved after the game.
suggestions.implemented_note: Git history is the audit trail. .github/workflows/verify.yml re-derives every number from the committed data on each push and fails if the published pages drift from the committed JSON, so a line cannot be quietly improved after the fact.

paths.name: Weekly commit at first kickoff
paths.pros: Simple, auditable, works with the CI already in place.
paths.cons: Depends on the job running on time.

paths.name: Signed tag per week
paths.pros: Cryptographic proof of when the line was fixed.
paths.cons: Extra ceremony for a single-owner repo.

paths.name: No freeze
paths.pros: Frictionless.
paths.cons: Destroys the credibility of every future grade. Not a real option.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Choose the freeze mechanism. Until then, treat all grades as provisional.

suggestions.title: Capture the official injury-report policy text
suggestions.problem: The engine needs a defensible mapping from practice status to whether a player suits up. The policy page returned an empty body (flag F06).

paths.name: Re-fetch with a rendering client and archive
paths.pros: Gives us the league's own wording.
paths.cons: Still a manual archive; may drift.

paths.name: Treat statuses as labels only, never as probabilities
paths.pros: Zero risk of asserting a rule that does not exist.
paths.cons: Kills the availability signal entirely.

paths.name: Use community-reported availability rates
paths.pros: Empirical, not doctrinal.
paths.cons: Not official, so it violates the project's own source rule.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Give the green light to archive an official copy, or accept a label-only model.

suggestions.title: Reconcile the Friday report against the 90-minute inactives
suggestions.problem: 185 of 345 Week 10 rows have a blank game status. We do not know whether blank means 'playing'.

paths.name: Collect the inactive list each week and measure
paths.pros: Turns a guess into a measured rate per status label.
paths.cons: Needs 8-10 weeks before the rate is trustworthy.

paths.name: Ignore blank-status rows entirely
paths.pros: No false precision. This is what v0 already does.
paths.cons: Misses genuine late-week scratches.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Approve weekly inactive capture, or accept that blank stays blank.

suggestions.title: Use snap counts as the depth-chart substitute
suggestions.problem: You asked to detect 2nd/3rd/4th string replacements. No official source publishes a depth ordinal (flag F05).

paths.name: Official participation counts as ordinal proxy
paths.pros: Official, quantitative, and directly measures who actually played.
paths.cons: Post-game, not predictive; needs the box score.

paths.name: Rank players by official season stat volume
paths.pros: Available from nfl.com player pages.
paths.cons: Volume is not depth; a WR2 with more targets than a WR1 breaks it.

paths.name: Say 'starter vs backup' only
paths.pros: Honest. No ordinal claimed.
paths.cons: Loses the 2nd/3rd/4th string distinction you asked for.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Accept participation counts as the ordinal, or accept a starter/backup binary.

suggestions.title: Decide the market-price question once, in writing
suggestions.problem: Every 'value' claim in betting requires a price. We hold none (flag F07).

paths.name: License an odds feed
paths.pros: Unlocks edge, CLV, and the Champion tier.
paths.cons: Cost, contract, and jurisdiction rules.

paths.name: Publish lines with no market comparison
paths.pros: Fully honest; the site already does this.
paths.cons: Cannot ever call a strategy 'good' in market terms.

paths.name: Compare to a public consensus number
paths.pros: Cheap proxy.
paths.cons: Unverifiable provenance; breaks the official-source rule.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Fund a feed, or accept that 'edge vs market' stays out of scope.

suggestions.title: Backtest and calibrate sigma before trusting any band
suggestions.problem: The line bands are derived from declared constants, not from observed error.

paths.name: Rebuild 2025 week-by-week and replay the engine
paths.pros: Real calibration: how often does the 90% band contain the result?
paths.cons: 18 weeks of manual capture.

paths.name: Keep declared constants and label them
paths.pros: Already done, already honest.
paths.cons: Bands stay unfalsified.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Authorise a historical rebuild, or keep bands clearly marked as uncalibrated.

suggestions.title: Dry-run the grading pipeline on Week 10
suggestions.problem: The leaderboard is empty because nothing has been graded. The pipeline itself is untested.

paths.name: Grade Week 10 as soon as the last game ends
paths.pros: Proves the pipeline end to end with 14 real games.
paths.cons: n=14 is far below any threshold; results prove plumbing, not skill.

paths.name: Wait for 30 games before grading anything
paths.pros: No misleading numbers.
paths.cons: Bugs stay undiscovered for weeks.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Approve a clearly-labelled plumbing test, or hold until the sample is meaningful.

suggestions.title: Settle whether luck-fading is real
suggestions.problem: The luck fade strategy (S04) is the counter-example the luck filter exists to catch. Nobody has tested whether fading lucky teams works.
suggestions.blocked_by: needs multi-season game-level history with prices

paths.name: Test on 3 prior seasons
paths.pros: Settles a decades-old market question with our own numbers.
paths.cons: Large lift; needs prices, which we do not have.

paths.name: Drop the luck-fade strategy
paths.pros: Removes a claim we cannot support.
paths.cons: Also removes a useful counter-example.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Fund the test, or keep S04 labelled as untested.

suggestions.title: Capture official player-game statistics
suggestions.problem: Every prop correlation magnitude is unmeasured without per-game player stats.

paths.name: Capture official box scores per game
paths.pros: Unlocks all prop work, plus snap-count cross-checks.
paths.cons: 345-row pages already large; box scores are bigger.

paths.name: Keep props blocked
paths.pros: Zero risk of a wrong correlation claim.
paths.cons: Player props were explicitly requested.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Approve box-score capture, or accept that props stay blocked.

suggestions.title: Signed weekly snapshots
suggestions.problem: Git history is good; cryptographic proof is better.

paths.name: Checksum each week's JSON into a published index
paths.pros: Anyone can verify a line was not changed after the fact.
paths.cons: Marginally more machinery.

paths.name: Rely on git history
paths.pros: Already works.
paths.cons: A force-push could rewrite it.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Pick checksum publication, or accept git as the only record.

suggestions.title: Choose the reward weighting explicitly
suggestions.problem: sqrt(n) normalisation rewards precision over volume, which is a values choice, not a fact.

paths.name: Precision-weighted (current)
paths.pros: Punishes volume-chasing; rewards selectivity, which is what you asked for.
paths.cons: Rewards abstention; a strategy that bets twice a year and wins both looks great.

paths.name: Total-profit-weighted
paths.pros: Intuitive.
paths.cons: Rewards volume; a lucky high-volume strategy beats a skilled selective one.

paths.name: Run both and publish a spread
paths.pros: Shows how much the ranking depends on the choice.
paths.cons: Two leaderboards to explain.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Confirm precision-weighting, or switch to profit-weighting.

suggestions.title: Capture game-by-game results with margins
suggestions.problem: No backtest is possible from season aggregates alone.

paths.name: Capture the scoreboard each week
paths.pros: Unlocks calibration, division tests, and real grading.
paths.cons: Weekly manual step until the refresh job handles it.

paths.name: Stay aggregate-only
paths.pros: No new work.
paths.cons: Every backtest stays parked.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Approve weekly scoreboard capture.

suggestions.title: Add turnover margin to the luck model
suggestions.problem: Pythagorean luck cannot separate takeaways from luck without turnover data.
suggestions.blocked_by: turnover margin not in the official standings table

paths.name: Derive from box scores
paths.pros: Completes the luck decomposition.
paths.cons: Depends on SG-10/SG-13 landing first.

paths.name: Accept an incomplete luck model
paths.pros: Already caveated on the site.
paths.cons: Some 'luck' is really takeaways.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Sequence SG-14 after box-score capture, or accept the caveat.

suggestions.title: Add venue and weather context
suggestions.problem: The Munich game is a neutral site, and outdoor totals depend on wind. Neither is in the model.

paths.name: Flag neutral-site games only
paths.pros: Fixes the biggest error (HFA applied at a neutral site).
paths.cons: Weather still absent.

paths.name: Full weather integration
paths.pros: Best totals.
paths.cons: Violates the official-source rule for one input.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Approve the neutral-site flag at minimum.

suggestions.title: Flag short weeks and byes
suggestions.problem: Thursday games and post-bye teams are invisible to a model that only sees season aggregates.

paths.name: Tag rest days from the schedule
paths.pros: Cheap, official, immediately usable.
paths.cons: Small effect, needs measurement before weighting.

paths.name: Ignore rest
paths.pros: Simpler.
paths.cons: Known bias left in.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Approve rest tagging.

suggestions.title: Test whether club-published depth charts are usable at all
suggestions.problem: The league does not publish a machine-checkable depth ordinal, but individual clubs sometimes publish dated depth charts. Whether those are consistent, timely, or stable enough to use has never been tested.

paths.name: Sample 4 clubs for 3 weeks and measure agreement
paths.pros: Produces a real number: how often do club charts agree with who actually started?
paths.cons: Club sites are not nfl.com, so any value derived this way may not meet the official-source rule.

paths.name: Skip club charts; use participation counts only
paths.pros: Keeps a single, official evidence standard.
paths.cons: Leaves a possible source unexplored.

suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Say whether club-published charts count as evidence, even though they are not nfl.com.

suggestions.title: Pick ONE canonical line series and freeze its sign convention
suggestions.problem: Three files publish a Week 10 line on two opposite conventions and disagree by 6.72 pts mean absolute (board/line-provenance.html). A reader gets a different answer depending on which page they open.

paths.name: Keep lines_week10.json and delete the other two
paths.pros: One file, one site, no reconciliation burden. The root site already renders it.
paths.cons: It is the WORST performer on the only settled sample (MAE 11.62 vs 8.02), and deleting 2026-week10-lines.csv removes the only market quotes in the repo.

paths.name: Switch to lines_origination.csv and label the other two deprecated
paths.pros: Better on the settled sample; its generator is the one with a documented calibration table; it is already labelled 'provisional, not bettable', which is honest.
paths.cons: n=12. Promoting on twelve games is exactly the result-chasing the gates exist to prevent, and it would be promoting on the same sample that was used to compare.

paths.name: Write a third, canonical engine and retire both
paths.pros: Lets the sign convention, the join key (game_id) and the dispersion fix be designed together rather than patched.
paths.cons: Slowest. Leaves the site publishing two inconsistent series in the meantime unless they are labelled.

suggestions.recommendation: C, with an immediate zero-cost action: label both live pages with the 6.72-pt discrepancy today, so no reader can mistake either for settled truth. Choosing between A and B on n=12 is a coin flip dressed as analysis.
suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Which series is 'our line'? (A keep json / B switch to csv / C new engine)

suggestions.title: Make capture a schedule with a clock on every row, and never overwrite a pre-kickoff read
suggestions.problem: The site is stamped 2026-11-14 and prices games played 2026-11-15. The same official URL read 48 hours apart gave LAC a game status on 0/19 rows then 9/19 (board/data-freshness.html). A single capture is a snapshot of a clock, not of the truth.

paths.name: Daily scheduled capture into data/captures/, append-only
paths.pros: Closes the staleness class of defect completely; gives the timestamped series the brief asks for; cheap because the pages are already readable.
paths.cons: Repository growth (~350 rows/day uncompressed) and a growing number of dated files to keep link-checked.

paths.name: Capture on the NFL's published report cadence only (Wed/Thu/Fri + game day)
paths.pros: Fewer files; matches when designations actually change.
paths.cons: Misses Saturday practice bumps and the Saturday IR moves that produced the Ravens' two added rows.

paths.name: External object store with hashes, repo keeps only an index
paths.pros: The durable-store requirement (R030) done properly; keeps raw rows out of the public artefact (R031).
paths.cons: Adds a dependency and a credential to manage, and blocks the whole pipeline if it is unavailable.

suggestions.recommendation: A now, C when the repo grows past a season. The one non-negotiable rule either way: never overwrite a pre-kickoff capture with a post-kickoff one, because the pre-kickoff read is the only evidence a backtest has.
suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: How often do we capture, and where does the immutable store live?

suggestions.title: Treat dispersion, not bias, as the top modelling priority
suggestions.problem: Across 11 pre-kickoff forecasts the model's margins have sd 3.41 while realised margins have sd 14.39 - a dispersion ratio of 0.24 (board/luck.html). Bias is +7.91 pts and accounts for only 28% of MSE. A near-constant forecast cannot beat a market however good its mean is.

paths.name: Re-centre only (remove the +7.91 bias)
paths.pros: Cheap; removes 28% of the squared error immediately.
paths.cons: Does not touch the 72% that is dispersion. Would improve MAE and change nothing about the ability to find an edge.

paths.name: Widen uncertainty with a game-specific variance model
paths.pros: Attacks the actual defect. Rest-day, travel, neutral-site, roof and divisional-vs-cross-conference are published schedule facts available today.
paths.cons: More parameters on a sample of 11 games; risks fitting noise and needs strict pre-registration.

paths.name: Keep a fixed sigma and stop quoting probabilities
paths.pros: Honest - if the model cannot express uncertainty, publishing only a point line with a wide band is defensible.
paths.cons: Gives up the proper-score leaderboard, which needs a probability.

suggestions.recommendation: B, pre-registered before the next scoring window, with A applied as a trivially safe first step. Do NOT tune anything on the current 11 games - they are the sample that produced the diagnosis and using them again would double-count.
suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Is dispersion the accepted top modelling priority, and is the variance model pre-registered before the next window?

suggestions.title: Replace fixed availability point-penalties with a pre-registered paired ablation
suggestions.problem: The engine subtracts fixed points per missing player by position (QB 2.6, CB 0.5, ...). Those constants are assumptions, not measurements, and depth rank does not tell us how much worse the replacement is (board/depth-evidence.html).

paths.name: Fit the per-position penalty from settled games
paths.pros: Still publishes one number per position, easy to explain.
paths.cons: Requires enough games with a clean before/after; with one week it would fit noise and become a new unvalidated constant.

paths.name: Paired ablation: identical model with and without availability features, chronological folds, interval on the difference
paths.pros: Answers the real question - does the availability signal add anything? - and reports uncertainty instead of a point estimate.
paths.cons: Cannot run until there is a multi-week snapshot series (SG-19) and a results corpus.

paths.name: Drop availability from the model until it can be validated
paths.pros: Most honest for immediate publication; removes four unvalidated constants.
paths.cons: Discards the one input the brief cares most about, and the availability signal is visibly real even if its size is unmeasured.

suggestions.recommendation: B as the target, C as the interim if the next scored week shows the constants hurting. Either way the constants should be labelled unvalidated on the lines page until an ablation clears them.
suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Target a paired ablation, or drop availability from the model until it can be validated?
suggestions.blocked_by: Needs a multi-week snapshot series (SG-19) and a results corpus

suggestions.title: Publish the requirement register as a decision queue, not a status list
suggestions.problem: 73 requirements with a status each is thorough but not actionable. Nothing currently says which single decision unblocks the most rows.

paths.name: Add a 'decisions that unblock the most rows' view
paths.pros: Turns 73 rows into about five named decisions; a reviewer can act in one sitting.
paths.cons: The unblock counts are heuristic and will be argued over.

paths.name: Add effort and owner columns
paths.pros: Standard project hygiene.
paths.cons: Does not reduce the reading burden, which is the actual problem.

paths.name: Leave it as-is
paths.pros: No work.
paths.cons: The brief explicitly asks for a page someone can review and choose from; a 73-row status table is not that.

suggestions.recommendation: A. The five decisions in the executive summary are the seed list.
suggestions.decision_needed_from_owner: Adopt the decision-queue view on top of the requirement register?

priority_order.why: Nothing can be graded, calibrated, or backtested without game-level results.
A grade is meaningless if the line can move after kickoff.
Decides whether 'edge' is ever in scope.
Unblocks every prop and correlation-magnitude question.
Turns the 2nd/3rd/4th-string request into something measurable.
Settles what a blank game status means.
The Munich game is currently mispriced by a full home-field advantage.
Answers whether a second, non-league depth source is even admissible under the source rule.
